purpose: Full-scene art-direction reference for diagnosing window geometry, interior/glass layering, and bloom; not an Unreal render or geometry measurement.
prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather and photorealistic-natural. Create ONE full-scene photographic target concept by editing the supplied actual Unreal Engine screenshot. The input is the exact fixed camera and architectural layout reference, not a loose inspiration. Preserve the image framing and wide landscape aspect ratio, camera position, perspective, all building silhouettes, every window and shutter location, balconies and ornate iron railings, red fabric awnings, narrow alley and ground. Do not redesign the scene or add people, vehicles, signs, new lamps or new objects. This is a proposed art-direction reference, not a diagram; no text or annotations.

Goal: convincing premium photorealistic nighttime Paris courtyard, with a coherent physically plausible photographic response to warm interiors seen through glass. Keep the currently illuminated rooms illuminated and the dark windows dark. Preserve the red awnings but make their brightness a believable consequence of nearby light. Cool dim night-sky fill, warm practical interior light, rich shadow depth with readable masonry texture; avoid the evenly lit grey daytime facade currently visible. Preserve material detail outside the bright windows rather than globally blurring the scene.

At illuminated windows, depict interior depth and just a few readable large silhouettes such as a table, curtains, shelves, with uneven light from practical lamps. Do NOT show a uniformly blurred orange image pasted on a pane or a sharp miniature dollhouse. Furniture should disappear progressively into reflections, curtains, veiling glare, highlight roll-off and glass scattering; not uniform Gaussian blur across the whole room. Warm bright cores near lamps, softer midtones farther inside. Pane glass has restrained night-sky reflections and subtle dirt/roughness, not opaque glowing paint.

Make lens bloom and halation clearly visible: a smooth multi-scale warm halo originates from the brightest portions of the windows and spills a little OVER adjacent dark window mullions and the outside edge of the window silhouette in screen space. A small near halo with a faint wider falloff; enough to look luminous at normal viewing size, not just sharp bright pixels bounded by a rectangle. Keep the mullion silhouettes readable beneath the bloom. Do not make the entire scene foggy or glow the whole building. Separately, plausible warm indirect illumination grazes nearby window reveals and sills with distance falloff.

Correct the erroneous razor-thin luminous line around the upper-right shuttered window: its top reveal and jambs must be solid non-emissive construction, not neon strips. Light must be occluded by frames/shutters. Distinguish legitimate soft optical bloom crossing silhouettes from actual geometric seams emitting light. No cracks filled with glowing material. Dark solid borders and real recess thickness, with gentle reflected light where appropriate.

Natural camera exposure, smooth filmic highlights, no clipped uniform white window rectangles, no candy orange saturation, no game HUD, no excessive anamorphic streaks. The result should be a full-scene realistic target for diagnosing lighting, glass, bloom, and window geometry while matching the screenshot composition very closely.
